title: Broad context supplied: same 3/22 CT instances, with recognition and coverage failures remaining
claim: On the same second CT case, a fresh Astra-medium context-supplied attempt recovered exactly the same 3/22 instances, 1/7 links and 2/15 events as the earlier image-only attempt. A separate CT-only probe inferred metastatic malignancy and included melanoma as a possibility while abstaining on exact hidden metadata. The new lesion trace explicitly rejected source GT2 at both visits as cyst-like/vascular and skipped all axial planes containing the small bone reference; these distinguish recognition disagreement from incomplete visual coverage.
limitations: One patient and one new attempt per condition; bundled context and stochastic variation are confounded.
The intervention supplies patient demographic metadata and cohort-level diagnosis/purpose only; individual clinical reports and surgical/treatment specifics are unavailable.
Clinical-context delivery is verified, but the public trace does not establish how the model used each supplied field.
Unknown exact metadata are not CT-inference failures; schema validity is not diagnostic correctness or calibration.
Recognition disagreements are relative to source GT, not independent clinical adjudication. Views containing a target do not establish attention.
Original scores, references and freezes remain unchanged; no additional model trial is launched.
